en: The Questions of King Milinda:
The Chapter on Similes,
Section on the Earth.
7. The Question on the Five Qualities of the Moon “Venerable Nāgasena, when you say that ‘five qualities of the moon should be adopted,’ which are those five qualities that should be adopted?
“Just as, O Great King, the moon, rising in the bright fortnight, increases more and more;”
In the same way, great king, a yogi, a practitioner of yoga, must increase further and further in the practice of conduct, virtue, qualities, and observances;

in the study of the scriptures and the attainment of realization; in seclusion, the foundations of mindfulness, guarding the doors of the sense faculties, moderation in eating, and devotion to wakefulness.
This, Great King, is the first quality of the moon that should be adopted.
Furthermore, Great King, the moon possesses a sublime sovereignty;
even so, Great King, a practitioner devoted to yoga should possess a sublime sovereignty of aspiration.
This, Great King, is the second quality of the moon that should be adopted.
Furthermore, Great King, the moon moves about at night;
even so, Great King, the practitioner of yoga should be secluded.
This, Great King, is the third quality of the moon that should be adopted.
Furthermore, Great King, the moon has a celestial palace as its banner;
even so, Great King, the practitioner of yoga should have virtue as his banner.
This, Great King, is the fourth quality of the moon that should be adopted.
Furthermore, Great King, the moon rises having been invoked and prayed for;
even so, Great King, a yogi, a practitioner of yoga, should approach families having been invoked and prayed for.
"This, Great King, is the fifth quality of the moon that should be adopted.

And this was said, Great King, by the Blessed One, the God above Gods, in the noble Saṃyutta Nikāya: 'Monks, approach families like the moon—keeping the body withdrawn, keeping the mind withdrawn, ever-new to the families, and free from arrogance.
The Seventh Question on the Qualities of the Moon.
